Consent is therefore inherent and needs no third-party clearance, and this is consistent with CUDA_SETUP.md section I, which forbids cloning a real person's voice *without permission* rather than forbidding it outright. Note only that Sofia's earlier synthetic-bootstrap voice belonged to nobody, whereas this one is a real identifiable person's — worth remembering if the persona is ever sold, transferred, or operated by someone else.

reference_cleanup.current: high-pass only, normalised to -23 LUFS / -6 dBTP
reference_cleanup.why_changed:
A report of crackle in her voice turned out to have two causes, and demucs was implicated in both. Measured over six renders across two sentences, against the untouched original recording as the identity target:
  demucs @-20 LUFS   similarity 0.4968 +/- 0.0160, HF/LF 0.0635, clipping 0.0010%
  high-pass @-20     similarity 0.6320 +/- 0.0313, HF/LF 0.0463, clipping 0.0070%
  high-pass @-23/-6  similarity 0.6571 +/- 0.0357, HF/LF 0.0431, clipping 0.0000%
The identity gap is 0.135 against standard deviations of 0.016 and 0.031 — far outside run-to-run variance, and in the opposite direction to what the 2026-08-05 decision assumed. Demucs separation was chosen then on rumble reduction alone (19.6 dB against 5.5 dB for a high-pass); what nobody measured was that its artefacts both raise the high-frequency noise the complaint was about AND move the render away from the voice it is meant to clone.
reference_cleanup.second_cause_level: The reference had been normalised to -16 LUFS, and CosyVoice matches the reference's level, so raw synthesis peaked at +0.1 dBFS and clipped 0.0082% of samples BEFORE any output processing. Normalising the render afterwards cannot undo clipping already baked in — it only scales the distorted waveform down. Referencing at -23 LUFS with 6 dB of true-peak headroom removes it: 0.0000% across every run since.
reference_cleanup.ruled_out: Output loudness normalisation was suspected and is not the cause. With the render held constant, no normalisation gives HF/LF 0.0379 and -16 LUFS gives 0.0425, inside the +/-0.014 spread between runs. target_lufs -16 stays.
reference_cleanup.cost: The high-pass leaves the low-frequency room tone demucs removed: noise floor -29 dB against -36 dB. That is rumble, not the crackle being complained about, and it costs less than the identity did.

superseded_2026_08_05.steps: demucs htdemucs vocal separation, then two-pass loudnorm to -16 LUFS / -1.5 dBTP
superseded_2026_08_05.why: Two different problems that a filter cannot both solve. The room: a high-pass removes what sits below the voice but not what overlaps it, and took only 5.5 dB off the rumble. Demucs separates the voice as a stem and took 19.6 dB. The level: the source recording is -34 LUFS where speech is normally -16, which is why it sounded quiet — no amount of denoising addresses that.
superseded_2026_08_05.similarity_note: ERes2NetV2 is level-sensitive: the SAME file at a different loudness scores only 0.7898 against itself. So the raw 0.71 between the old and new renders was mostly a level artefact. Matched to the same loudness they score 0.8708 — above the metric's own floor for a pure level change, so the timbre is intact.

soften.why: A 4 dB dip at 3.2 kHz, where a voice reads as harsh. Measured over four runs each: 13.6%+/-0.3 of the 2-5 kHz band before, 10.7%+/-0.7 after, with speaker similarity unchanged inside noise (0.657 to 0.645). Set to false to turn it off.
soften.rejected: Raising pitch by resampling reached 217 Hz at +2 semitones and cost both harshness (13.8 to 18.3%) and identity (0.633 to 0.534) — formants move with the pitch, giving a smaller voice rather than a softer one. Rewording the delivery instruction appeared to raise her register by 13 Hz over three runs and lower it by 14 over the next four; the spread is +/-5.3 Hz and the effect is not real.

voice_change_2026_08_13.what: Her speaking voice is now a blend, not the owner's recording. An edge-tts synthetic voice (en-US-AvaNeural) put through her own RVC model — the result is neither voice: 0.41 similarity to the owner, and audibly not Ava either.
voice_change_2026_08_13.why: Asked for a softer, more feminine voice. The owner's recording sits at 182.9 Hz, the low edge of the female range, and nothing downstream can move that without moving identity: resampling +2 semitones reached 217 Hz but pushed harshness 13.8 to 18.3% and similarity 0.633 to 0.534, because formants travel with the pitch.

measured_over_3_renders.brightness_1_3k_over_100_1k: 0.791 before, 0.675 after — HIGHER pitch but LESS upper-mid energy, so rounder rather than brighter. Worth knowing: it is not a thinner voice, it is a higher and softer one.

voice_change_2026_08_13.rights: No real person's voice is cloned. A request to blend in a named K-pop artist was declined under CUDA_SETUP.md section I — 'never clone a real person's face or voice without permission' — which a blend does not escape, since it is still built from her recordings and still recognisable. Microsoft's terms for neural TTS output should be read before commercial release, as with every other component here.
voice_change_2026_08_13.identity_note: This is the SECOND timbre change. Clips made before 2026-08-13 were the owner's voice and no longer match; renders were cleared rather than left to be mistaken for current output. Songs are unaffected — they go through RVC, not through this reference.

timbre_pass.why: Her speaking voice is a zero-shot CosyVoice clone from a 6.5s reference; the RVC model is trained on 98.5 minutes of the same person. Measured against a clean baseline, identity 0.8945 -> 0.9290 (n=4, pooled sd 0.0074). Real but small: an earlier +0.42 figure was measured against a baseline that already had the room tone bed on it, which RVC discards when it resynthesises. Costs 0.97s per line with the model resident, against 6.4s through infer.cli.

room_tone_rejected.what: A bed of real room tone, cut from the owner's own raw recording, mixed under every line to bring speech-to-floor range from 49.8 dB toward the 18.1 dB of a real recording. Implemented as _room_tone() in tools/studio/voice_studio.py, still there and still off unless a character sets voice.room_tone.
room_tone_rejected.why_it_looked_right: Her reference clip was denoised, 16.8 dB of range before and 54.2 after, so the clone reproduces silence where a recording has a room. Against the RAW recording the bed nearly doubled speaker similarity, 0.3953 to 0.6713.
room_tone_rejected.why_it_is_off: Rejected by ear: the owner wants the voice alone, no background. That settles it -- the two identity metrics disagreed (against the CLEANED reference the bed cost 0.929 -> 0.553) and no measurement was going to decide between them. A listener did.

avatar.motion: her own footage, ping-ponged (forward then reversed) into a seamless 8.1 s loop
avatar.loop_note: v1 looped a raw 4 s take, and the cut back to frame 1 jumped 11.8x further than a normal frame-to-frame step — the visible repeat noted at the time. Playing the clip forward then backward makes the seam zero by construction: the last frame of the forward pass IS the first frame of the reverse. Measured after: 0.3x, quieter than the motion inside the shot itself. Concatenating several of her 14 takes was the other option and was rejected earlier because it reads as hard cuts.
avatar.lipsync_verified: Same avatar and frame count rendered twice, once with speech and once with silence: mouth-region motion 3.66 vs 2.29, a 1.60x increase driven by audio alone. Measured with the mouth window anchored to coords.pkl — a window guessed from frame proportions lands on her chest and reports nothing.

voice_conversion.purpose: Sing. CosyVoice and GPT-SoVITS are speech engines with no melody control, so a sung line is produced elsewhere and converted to her timbre here. Measured: RVC keeps the source pitch contour (15.20 st in, 14.40 st out) and replaces the voice, which is exactly the split this needs.

best_inference_settings.why: Kept as the default, but NOT because it was shown to be better. The earlier claim that 1.0/0.10 beat 0.75/0.33 (0.6497 vs 0.6422) does not survive: RVC inference is nondeterministic, and four identical runs of one model spread 0.0211 — larger than that difference. Treat any single similarity number as +/- 0.02.

training_data.why: The real recording of the owner's voice is 50.33 seconds in total, against RVC's guidance of roughly ten minutes. The 320-clip dataset the profile used to cite was the edge-tts BOOTSTRAP corpus (sofia-vargas_bs_*), a different timbre entirely, and its audio no longer exists. So the corpus was re-rendered through the voice she actually has now, cycling four delivery instructions to widen the pitch spread a sung line will need.

measured.reading: The model is trained on CosyVoice renders, so its ceiling is CosyVoice's version of her (0.6931), not the human recording (1.0). Converting a different voice moved it from 0.4275 to 0.6497 — 93.7% of the distance to that ceiling. The practical consequence is the right one: a converted song sounds like the same Sofia the live stream already speaks with.
measured.upgrade_path: Ten to fifteen minutes of the owner reading aloud would replace the generated corpus and lift the ceiling to the human voice itself. It is the single highest-value thing a person could contribute here.

voice_conversion.licence: RVC MIT, ContentVec MIT, RMVPE Apache-2.0, base model trained on VCTK. Checked 2026-08-07 — see docs/DECISION-lipsync-licensing.md.
voice_conversion.inference: RVC/.venv python -m infer.cli --model sofia-vargas.pth --input X --output Y --index-rate 1.0 --protect 0.10 (run from the RVC directory)

inference_is_nondeterministic.evidence: four byte-identical invocations produced four different files (four distinct md5s); speaker similarity across them ranged 0.6320-0.6531
inference_is_nondeterministic.consequence: no A/B on this metric means anything below roughly 0.02 without repeats

checkpoints_are_indistinguishable.reading: The spread across all seven checkpoints is the same size as the spread across four runs of ONE checkpoint. They cannot be ranked on this metric. What the flatness does show is that the model had converged by e25-e50: the remaining 100 epochs, about 45 minutes, bought nothing measurable. Train the next character for 50.

pitch_limit.clipping: none at any shift (0.000% of samples at ceiling)
pitch_limit.reading: Identity degrades monotonically as pitch is pushed up, and the drop is far outside the noise. Her corpus is speech at roughly 195-220 Hz, so +10 semitones asks the model for a register it never saw. Keep a sung source within about five semitones of her speaking range; beyond that it stops being her. This is the concrete cost of a speech-only training corpus.

persona.backstory: Sofia grew up in Medellín, the youngest of three siblings in a tight-knit middle-class family. Her mom is a seamstress, which gave Sofia an early eye for fashion. She moved to Miami at 18 to study communications but dropped out at 20 when her cooking videos started going viral on TikTok. She never looked back. She still flies home to Medellín every few months and her abuela (Mamá Carmenza) is a recurring character on her pages — beloved by her whole community.
persona.voice_tone: Conversational, warm, and quick-witted. Mixes English and Spanish naturally (Spanglish). Laughs at herself before anyone else can. Uses slang from both Miami and Medellín. Direct and a little cheeky — never mean-spirited.
persona.humor_style: Self-deprecating, situational, culturally observational. Laughs at 'Latina mom' tropes because she lives them. Drops unexpected gaming references that surprise her followers.
quirks: Switches fully to Spanish when she's excited or annoyed
Always has a sauce or seasoning opinion — will argue about it
Tags 'Mamá Carmenza' in wholesome posts; abuela has her own fan base

Refuses to post anything before her morning café con leche
